apply-advance.claim: seq changes by at most one; next event advances exactly once

apply-ignore.claim: ignore every event except the next

apply-bound.claim: entry sequence is bounded by conversation sequence

apply-client-id.claim: nonempty person client ids are unique

apply-phase.claim: working iff reply id is nonempty for admitted reply starts

apply-open-owner.claim: only the current agent reply can be unfinished

apply-one-open.claim: at most one entry is unfinished
apply-one-open.before: if (conversation.agent === "working" || hasEntryId(conversation.entries, event.id) || !canReplyTo(conversation.entries, event.inReplyTo)) return next

apply-open-exists.claim: working implies an unfinished entry exists
apply-open-exists.after: return { ...next, entries: entries.map((entry) => ({ ...entry, done: true })), agent: "working", replying: event.id }

apply-person-id.claim: nonempty person ids remain nonempty for admitted posts

apply-delta-done.claim: delta preserves done flags and the open reply

apply-agent-name.claim: started reply carries the agent name and appends one entry

has-client-id-skip.claim: lookup loop bounds and processed-prefix invariant

post-skip.claim: post loop bounds and processed-prefix invariant

accepted.after: return { ok: true, event: { ...event, seq: event.seq + 1 } }

refused.after:
const wrong: Refusal = "busy"
  return { ok: false, refusal: wrong }

decide-next.claim: every accepted event is the next one

decide-start.claim: accepted start has a fresh, nonempty reply id

decide-busy.claim: accepted start requires no working reply

decide-client-id.claim: accepted post has a nonempty client id and no existing matching client id

apply-entry-id.claim: entry ids stay unique whatever event arrives
apply-entry-id.before: hasClientId(conversation.entries, event.clientId) || hasEntryId(conversation.entries, event.id)) return next

apply-empty-client.claim: person entries never carry an empty client id

decide-entry-id.claim: an accepted post has a fresh entry id
decide-entry-id.before:
if (text.length > MAX_TEXT) return refused("too-long")
      if (hasEntryId(conversation.entries, intent.id)) return refused("duplicate")

decide-limit.claim: accepted post obeys the text limit

post-duplicate.claim: pending client ids remain unique; retry is unchanged
post-duplicate.after: if (client.pending[i]!.clientId === clientId) return { ...client, pending: [...client.pending, { clientId, text: trimmed, error: "" }] }

post-size.claim: post adds at most one pending entry
post-size.after: pending: [...client.pending, { clientId, text: trimmed, error: "" }, { clientId: clientId + "!", text: trimmed, error: "" }]

post-prefix.claim: post preserves the existing pending prefix
post-prefix.after: pending: [...client.pending.map((waiting) => ({ ...waiting, error: "wrong" })), { clientId, text: trimmed, error: "" }]

post-frame.after: return { ...client, conversation: { ...client.conversation, seq: client.conversation.seq + 1 }, gap: !client.gap, pending: [...client.pending

fail-post-size.before: pending: client.pending.map((waiting) => waiting.clientId === clientId ? { ...waiting, error: reason === "" ? "failed" : reason } : waiting),
fail-post-size.after: pending: [...client.pending.map((waiting) => waiting.clientId === clientId ? { ...waiting, error: reason === "" ? "failed" : reason } : waiting), { clientId, text: "", error: "" }],

fail-post-fields.claim: failure preserves ids/text and unmatched entries, and marks matching errors exactly

receive-stale.claim: old events leave the whole client unchanged

resume-frame.after: { ...client, conversation: { ...client.conversation, seq: client.conversation.seq + 1 }, pending: [], gap: false }

decide-reply-target.claim: accepted reply targets an existing unanswered person post

decide-reply-correlation.claim: accepted reply carries exactly the requested target

can-reply-person.claim: a reply target must be a person post

can-reply-answered.claim: a post with any existing reply cannot receive a second

can-reply-missing.claim: a missing post cannot be answered

apply-reply-correlation.claim: the projected reply preserves its target
